newsitem.title: USA: NY man accused of hiding lottery winnings.
newsitem.headline: NY man accused of hiding lottery winnings.

text.p: A New York man, whose colleagues trusted him to buy their weekly lottery tickets, was accused on Wednesday of winning more than $700,000 and not sharing the news -- or the money -- with his co-workers.
Hector Ospina, who bought one of five winning tickets in the state's Dec. 21, 1996, Lotto drawing, faces charges of grand larceny and up to 25 years in prison if convicted.
Nine of Ospina's co-workers at an Estee Lauder factory in suburban Melville, New York, gave him $5 apiece to buy lottery tickets each week, authorities said.
He bought 10 tickets for the Dec. 21 drawing and won $1.4 million which he split with a friend, authorities said.
But he told some co-workers he hadn't bought any tickets, and he told others he used his own money, authorities said.
Because he had been buying the tickets for years, no one was suspicious, authorities said. He worked at the factory 11 years.
However, one colleague noticed a small item in a local newspaper identifying Ospina as a Lotto winner, they said.
Also, the group had been playing the same numbers -- 6, 10, 11, 13, 30, 36 -- for several months and realised Ospina had won, officials said. The co-workers contacted an attorney.
When Ospina was arrested at his home in Huntington, New York, late on Tuesday, he was carrying an airplane ticket for a Wednesday flight to Colombia in his pocket, authorities said.
Ospina, 37, worked as a mechanic at the factory. He is the father of a 6-year-old girl and a 5-month-old boy.
He was arraigned in a Suffolk County court and held on $300,000 bail. Officials also froze his bank account.

The total pot in the Dec. 21 drawing was $25 million, and Ospina's share after taxes was $1.4 million, which he said he split with his friend, authorities said. The co-workers want all $1.4 million back, their attorney said.
"They were shocked," said the attorney, Kevin Brosnahan. "They were betrayed by someone they worked with for 11 years."
